name: הֵימָן
summary: Heman son of Joel, grandson of Samuel, a Levite of Kohath, whom David set over the song in the house of Yahweh, “the king's seer in the words of God”, with Asaph and Jeduthun (1Ch 6:18; 15:17, 19; 25:1, 4–6; 2Ch 5:12); and Heman, one of the wise men with whom Solomon is compared, a son of Mahol (1Ki 5:11), named among the sons of Zerah of Judah (1Ch 2:6), to whom Psalm 88 is ascribed as “Heman the Ezrahite”. The spelling, with ה and no א, matches the Aramaic haphel הֵימִן “trust” (Dan 6:24) and its participle מְהֵימַן “faithful” (Dan 6:5), so the name may mean “faithful”; but a Hebrew name with an Aramaic form is unusual, and the root is not certain.

evidence.note: “Heman the singer, the son of Joel, the son of Samuel.”
“All these were the sons of הֵימָן the king's seer in the words of God.”
Solomon “was wiser than all men, than Ethan the Ezrahite, וְהֵימָן, Calcol and Darda, the sons of Mahol”.
“The sons of Zerah: Zimri, Ethan, וְהֵימָן, Calcol and Dara.”
“Because הֵימִן in his God”: the Aramaic haphel spelled with ה and י, as the name.

note: Takes a.dy.as (17 tokens). The zero-token cross-reference e.bh.ae (“הֵימָן see אמן”) is left unassigned. Whether the wise man of 1Ki 5:11 and the son of Zerah of 1Ch 2:6 are one man (TIPNR keeps two records) is not decided here; both are named. The tie to אמן rests on the form alone.
